title: Keystroke
subtitle: Multiplayer typing races, live
description: Share a room code and race friends in real-time, no sign-up. A Redis leaderboard pushes rank changes as people type. The whole stack runs in Docker.

sections.heading: WHY THIS EXISTS
sections.content: I wanted to actually learn Redis and sockets past the tutorial level, and a typing race is a good excuse — it needs a live leaderboard, fast state updates, and rooms that don't step on each other.

sections.heading: THE HARD PART
sections.content: Every keystroke updating the leaderboard for everyone in the room would've drowned the client. I throttled progress updates instead of sending on every character, and used a Redis sorted set so rank changes stay cheap to compute even as more players join.

sections.heading: WHAT CHANGED IN MY HEAD
sections.content: Not everything needs a database. Rooms are short-lived, so I kept the whole thing in Redis with no persistent storage — a deliberate choice, not a shortcut, once I actually thought about what the data needed to outlive.

sections.heading: WORTH POINTING AT
bulletPoints: Redis sorted set leaderboard broadcasting live rank updates over Socket.IO
8-character room codes with lookalike characters removed, resolved server-side so the client never handles raw contest IDs
No persistent database — an intentional call given how short-lived a room is
Full stack containerized with Docker Compose for dev/prod parity
